es: Detectar afirmaciones sin fuente en un mensaje, reescribirlas con atribución y cautela, y justificar cada cambio.

teaching.en: The post says the school will close, but it is only a rumour.
teaching.es: La publicación dice que el colegio cerrará, pero es solo un rumor.
teaching.explanationEs: Sin fuente ni pruebas, una afirmación es un rumor aunque se escriba como un hecho.
segments: The post says the school will close,
but it is only a rumour.
teaching.audioText: The post says the school will close, but it is only a rumour.

teaching.en: Before you share the message, verify the claim with a reliable source.
teaching.es: Antes de compartir el mensaje, verifica la afirmación con una fuente fiable.
teaching.explanationEs: Verify es el primer paso del chequeo: buscar la fuente original antes de repetir el dato.
segments: Before you share the message, verify
the claim with a reliable source.
teaching.audioText: Before you share the message, verify the claim with a reliable source.

teaching.en: Obviously, the new rule is unfair.
teaching.es: Obviamente, la nueva norma es injusta.
teaching.explanationEs: Obviously y everyone knows presentan una opinión como si fuera un hecho: es la señal clásica de una afirmación sin fuente.
teaching.audioText: Obviously, the new rule is unfair.

teaching.en: Apparently, the school will close in June, but there is no proof yet.
teaching.es: Al parecer, el colegio cerrará en junio, pero todavía no hay pruebas.
teaching.explanationEs: Apparently da el dato con cautela. Proof es incontable: there is no proof, no «there are no proofs».
segments: Apparently, the school will close in June,
but there is no proof yet.
teaching.audioText: Apparently, the school will close in June, but there is no proof yet.

teaching.en: These numbers suggest that the school may lose pupils next year.
teaching.es: Estas cifras apuntan a que el colegio podría perder alumnos el año próximo.
teaching.explanationEs: Suggest + that + may: dos formas de cautela juntas, apropiadas cuando hay indicios pero no una confirmación.
segments: These numbers suggest that the school
teaching.audioText: These numbers suggest that the school may lose pupils next year.

teaching.en: An unverified message is not a fact until a source confirms it.
teaching.es: Un mensaje sin verificar no es un hecho hasta que una fuente lo confirma.
teaching.explanationEs: Unverified dice con claridad que el dato no está comprobado; es mejor que callar la duda.
segments: An unverified message is not a
fact until a source confirms it.

prompt.es: Elige la frase del texto que es una afirmación sin fuente.

choices.text: Everyone knows it is the best in the country.
The town library opens at nine, according to its website.
The mayor said the library will get new books in May.

feedback.es: Everyone knows no nombra fuente ni pruebas; las otras dos frases atribuyen el dato a una web y a la alcaldesa.

origin.text: The town library opens at nine, according to its website. Everyone knows it is the best in the country. The mayor said the library will get new books in May.

prompt.es: Reescribe las tres afirmaciones del mensaje y justifica cada cambio.

answer.text: 1. According to a letter from the council, the school may close in June, but nobody has confirmed the date. 2. Apparently the director might leave, but there is no proof yet, so this news is unverified. 3. Some parents say the canteen food is not good, and a health report suggests that the menu needs more fruit. I changed the first sentence because it had no source. I changed the second one because it sounded too certain. I changed the third one because it gave an opinion as a fact.
accepted: 1. According to a letter from the council, the school may close in June, but nobody has confirmed the date. 2. Apparently the director might leave, but there is no proof yet, so this news is unverified. 3. Some parents say the canteen food is not good, and a health report suggests that the menu needs more fruit. I changed the first sentence because it had no source. I changed the second one because it sounded too certain. I changed the third one because it gave an opinion as a fact.

First, the letter from the council says that the school could close in June, so I added the source. Second, there is no proof that the director is leaving, so I wrote that it is only a rumour and that nobody has confirmed it. Third, I do not know if the canteen food is bad, but some parents say it is, and a report suggests that more fruit is needed. I changed each claim because the original message gave no sources and sounded certain.

feedback.es: Un buen chequeo reescribe cada afirmación con fuente o cautela y explica por qué: sin fuente, sin pruebas o con opinión presentada como hecho.
